purpose: Deterministic event-driven research/live trading engine; useful patterns for point-in-time replay, orchestration, adapters, risk and causal clocks.
latencySuitability: HIGH: Rust-native async engine, nanosecond event model and modular live adapters; live US-equity depth/coverage still depends on an entitled provider such as Databento or a broker adapter.
maintenance: Very active. Repository metadata showed a push on 2026-08-28 and active v2 development; large established project with CI across master/nightly/develop.
docsTests: README documents deterministic research/live parity, quote/trade/order-book replay and modular adapters. Core time implementation was inspected: it explicitly separates monotonic real-time from manually controlled static simulation time, which is directly relevant to TAGX causal replay.
securityNotes: Strong upstream controls documented: protected branches, signed commits/releases, cargo-vet/cargo-deny, CodeQL, OSV/pip/cargo audits, fuzzing, pinned Actions, SLSA provenance and signed images. Direct adoption would materially expand TAGX's Rust/Python dependency and runtime surface.
dataCostNotes: Engine itself is open source, but actionable US-equity streaming/order-book data requires third-party provider entitlements and associated cost/licensing.
lookAheadBiasRisk: LOW when its static clock/event-time semantics are preserved; misuse remains possible if TAGX final mover labels are injected into signal-time event streams.
integrationPlan: Do not add as a production dependency. Borrow deterministic dual-clock/event-time patterns for Missed-Mover Replay and champion/challenger parity. Consider sandbox adapter benchmark only after a licensed streaming feed is selected.
whyNotIntegrateNow: TAGX's immediate failure mode is causal market-baseline integrity, not lack of a full execution engine. A direct Nautilus dependency would add complexity without fixing today's data error.
evidenceReviewed: repository metadata and current maintenance state
